index_candidates.name: Big Mac Index
index_candidates.short_description: Uses a standardized burger to illustrate purchasing-power parity and relative currency valuation.
index_candidates.claimed_interpretation: A readable proxy for PPP gaps rather than a full currency model.
index_candidates.commercial_reader_hook: Can a burger tell you whether a currency is cheap?

index_candidates.name: Starbucks Latte Index
index_candidates.short_description: Compares the price of a standardized coffee drink across cities or countries.
index_candidates.underlying_signal: urban cost of living and wage structure
index_candidates.claimed_interpretation: A consumer-friendly price lens on city affordability.
index_candidates.commercial_reader_hook: How expensive is a city if you measure it in lattes?

index_candidates.name: iPhone Work-Time Index
index_candidates.short_description: Measures how many working hours or days are needed to buy an iPhone.
index_candidates.claimed_interpretation: Affordability is clearer in hours worked than in dollar prices.
index_candidates.commercial_reader_hook: The same phone can cost 25 hours of work in one country and 160 in another.

index_candidates.name: IKEA Billy Index
index_candidates.short_description: Uses a standardized furniture item to compare local purchasing conditions.
index_candidates.underlying_signal: retail pricing, logistics and income differences
index_candidates.claimed_interpretation: A durable-goods analogue to burger-based affordability comparisons.
index_candidates.period_history: concept repeated in the source pack
index_candidates.commercial_reader_hook: A bookshelf can reveal trade costs better than a burger.

index_candidates.name: Haircut Index
index_candidates.short_description: Tracks the affordability of a local service whose price is labor-heavy and location-specific.
index_candidates.underlying_signal: service wages, rent and urban cost structure
index_candidates.claimed_interpretation: Services often expose local labor costs better than tradable goods do.
index_candidates.period_history: repeated concept in the source pack
index_candidates.commercial_reader_hook: A haircut may tell you more about a city than a burger does.

index_candidates.name: Taxi Affordability Index
index_candidates.short_description: Compares the affordability of a standard city ride.
index_candidates.underlying_signal: fuel, regulation, labor and urban friction
index_candidates.claimed_interpretation: Mobility is a lived cost that readers can picture immediately.
index_candidates.period_history: proposed repeatedly in the source pack
index_candidates.commercial_reader_hook: How many minutes of work does a routine ride consume?

index_candidates.name: Hotel Room Index
index_candidates.short_description: Uses a standard hotel night to compare tourism-driven city costs.
index_candidates.underlying_signal: tourism intensity, property prices and seasonality
index_candidates.claimed_interpretation: A one-night stay becomes a readable urban inflation metric.
index_candidates.commercial_reader_hook: What does one normal night cost in local work time?

index_candidates.name: Date Night Index
index_candidates.short_description: Bundles dinner, drinks, transport and entertainment into one lifestyle affordability metric.
index_candidates.claimed_interpretation: Composite leisure affordability can be more vivid than CPI slices.
index_candidates.period_history: recurring composite candidate in the source pack
index_candidates.commercial_reader_hook: How expensive is a normal evening out where you live?

index_candidates.name: Lipstick Index
index_candidates.short_description: Suggests consumers buy small luxuries in bad times instead of larger discretionary goods.
index_candidates.claimed_interpretation: Interesting behavioral hypothesis, weak as a predictive law.
index_candidates.commercial_reader_hook: Can lipstick sales tell you a recession is here?

index_candidates.name: Men’s Underwear Index
index_candidates.short_description: Claims men delay replacing underwear during hard times, making sales a stress indicator.
index_candidates.claimed_interpretation: Memorable and plausible-sounding, but not strongly proven.
index_candidates.commercial_reader_hook: Underwear sales are a ridiculous and memorable test of economic stress.

index_candidates.name: Second-hand Index
index_candidates.short_description: Uses resale activity as a signal of squeezed incomes or shifting consumption values.
index_candidates.claimed_interpretation: Resale markets may reveal both pressure and preference change.
index_candidates.commercial_reader_hook: A thriving resale market can mean thrift, stress or fashion—sometimes all three.

index_candidates.name: Working Hours Index
index_candidates.short_description: Converts prices into working time rather than currency.
index_candidates.underlying_signal: wages translated into lived purchasing effort
index_candidates.claimed_interpretation: Working hours are often the clearest affordability language for readers.
index_candidates.commercial_reader_hook: The real price of a thing is how much of your life it consumes.

index_candidates.name: Minimum Wage Meal Index
index_candidates.short_description: Measures how many simple meals can be bought from a minimum wage.
index_candidates.claimed_interpretation: A sharper inequality story than average wages alone.
index_candidates.commercial_reader_hook: How many basic lunches fit inside one legal minimum hour of work?

index_candidates.name: Rent-to-Burger Index
index_candidates.short_description: Expresses rent in units of familiar consumer goods or work time.
index_candidates.underlying_signal: housing burden translated into readable units
index_candidates.claimed_interpretation: Housing becomes more tangible when it is restated in everyday units.
index_candidates.commercial_reader_hook: How many burgers does a month of rent actually cost?

index_candidates.name: Baltic Dry Index
index_candidates.short_description: Tracks the cost of shipping major dry bulk commodities by sea.
index_candidates.underlying_signal: physical trade and commodity shipping demand
index_candidates.claimed_interpretation: A grounded signal of the physical economy rather than consumer sentiment.
index_candidates.commercial_reader_hook: The price of moving coal and grain can tell a different story than the price of a burger.

index_candidates.name: Container Freight Index
index_candidates.short_description: Measures container shipping costs across major routes.
index_candidates.claimed_interpretation: Shows how the goods economy can spike before consumer shelves tell the story.
index_candidates.commercial_reader_hook: A sofa or smartphone may get expensive long before CPI fully notices.

index_candidates.name: Skyscraper Index
index_candidates.short_description: Links the completion of record-breaking skyscrapers to crises or downturns.
index_candidates.underlying_signal: ambition and late-cycle excess, if anything
index_candidates.claimed_interpretation: Excellent narrative object, weak as a clean predictive tool.
index_candidates.commercial_reader_hook: Do the tallest buildings arrive right before the fall?

index_candidates.name: Restaurant Reservation Index
index_candidates.short_description: Uses near-real-time dining demand as a pulse of consumer activity.
index_candidates.claimed_interpretation: A nowcasting-style behavior signal rather than a durable structural index.
index_candidates.commercial_reader_hook: How busy restaurants are can become a real-time mood ring for a city.

index_candidates.name: Electricity Demand Index
index_candidates.short_description: Uses electricity consumption as a proxy for industrial and commercial activity.
index_candidates.claimed_interpretation: A grounded operational signal that can complement price-based measures.
index_candidates.commercial_reader_hook: A city’s power draw can be one of the cleanest clues to whether it is really humming.

index_candidates.name: Cigarette Equivalent Air Pollution Index
index_candidates.short_description: Translates PM2.5 exposure into an intuitive cigarette-equivalent risk analogy.
index_candidates.underlying_signal: air-pollution exposure translated into a familiar unit
index_candidates.claimed_interpretation: Powerful for communication if clearly framed as analogy, not literal smoking equivalence.
index_candidates.commercial_reader_hook: Three cigarettes of pollution is instantly felt in a way 66 micrograms per cubic meter is not.

index_candidates.name: CO2 Flight Equivalent Index
index_candidates.short_description: Restates carbon emissions in flights, cars or similar familiar units.
index_candidates.claimed_interpretation: Translation can make emissions legible, but coefficients and boundaries must be explicit.
index_candidates.period_history: translation family, not one canonical benchmark
index_candidates.commercial_reader_hook: A ton of CO2 means more when turned into flights or cars.

index_candidates.name: AI Index
index_candidates.short_description: A large composite report tracking the development, adoption and governance of AI.
index_candidates.claimed_interpretation: Useful as a modern benchmark family, but much heavier and more political than a single affordability proxy.
index_candidates.commercial_reader_hook: Some indices now rank not burgers or freight, but the future of intelligence itself.

index_candidates.name: Government AI Readiness Index
index_candidates.short_description: Ranks governments by readiness to deploy AI.
index_candidates.claimed_interpretation: A governance benchmark rather than a direct lived-economy translation.
index_candidates.commercial_reader_hook: Even states now compete through indices that try to quantify intelligence readiness.

index_candidates.name: SWE-Bench
index_candidates.short_description: Benchmarks model performance on software engineering tasks.
index_candidates.underlying_signal: AI coding capability under a structured benchmark
index_candidates.claimed_interpretation: Useful as a chapter-edge case showing how benchmark culture itself becomes an index world.
index_candidates.commercial_reader_hook: Some of the strangest modern indices no longer rank cities or prices—they rank machines.

story_candidates.hook: A burger became one of the most famous unofficial currency tools in the world.
story_candidates.why_interesting: It shows how a ridiculous-seeming consumer object can survive because it compresses a hard theory into a simple comparison.
story_candidates.possible_chapter_role: Opening proof that readable indices can travel farther than precise models.

story_candidates.hook: Prices in dollars are less revealing than prices in hours of life.
story_candidates.why_interesting: It turns purchasing power into time, which feels concrete and emotionally legible.
story_candidates.possible_chapter_role: Core thesis cluster for affordability chapters.

story_candidates.hook: Air pollution becomes readable when translated into cigarettes, but dangerous if the analogy is oversold.
story_candidates.why_interesting: This is one of the strongest examples of translation beating raw units for public comprehension.

story_candidates.hook: Some unusual indices are memorable because they are weak, not because they are true.
story_candidates.why_interesting: It gives the book tension: strange indices can clarify or deceive.

story_candidates.hook: A burger and a ship can tell opposite sides of the same economy.
story_candidates.why_interesting: It connects lived consumer prices with the deep physical plumbing of trade.
story_candidates.possible_chapter_role: Bridge chapter from popular to serious market signals.

story_candidates.hook: A city becomes legible when measured in lattes, taxis, haircuts and one normal night out.
story_candidates.why_interesting: It gives readers a relatable cluster rather than one-off novelty.

story_candidates.hook: One object is noisy; a basket of strange objects can become sturdier.
story_candidates.why_interesting: It opens the path from playful index to real methodology.

story_candidates.hook: Once an index becomes a target, it may stop measuring what it promised.
story_candidates.why_interesting: It broadens the book from playful comparisons to governance and manipulation failures.
story_candidates.possible_chapter_role: Late warning chapter on benchmark corruption.

story_candidates.hook: Readers can learn not just to consume indices, but to design them.
story_candidates.why_interesting: It turns the book from catalog into method.

story_candidates.hook: Modern AI culture is producing its own strange index ecosystem.

story_candidates.why_interesting: It preserves credibility without collapsing into product marketing.

story_candidates.hook: Carbon, pollution and water become more morally vivid when translated into familiar units.
story_candidates.why_interesting: The translation itself is the story: good translation informs, bad translation manipulates.

story_candidates.hook: Reservations, freight and electricity can function like a live nervous system for the economy.
story_candidates.why_interesting: These are timely, operational and feel more real than abstract annual statistics.

claims.claim: Big Mac Index is a useful illustration of PPP deviations, but not a complete currency valuation model.
Working-hours comparisons are often more meaningful to readers than simple cross-country dollar prices.
A basket or median of several comparable items is more robust than relying on a single consumer product.
Lipstick Index is better treated as a media-friendly hypothesis than as a dependable predictor.
Men’s Underwear Index is memorable but weakly evidenced as a formal macro signal.
Baltic Dry Index has a stronger claim to economic grounding than the folklore indicator family.
Cigarette-equivalent pollution is a risk analogy, not a literal statement that breathing polluted air equals smoking the same chemical dose.
PM2.5 concentration, AQI, annual exposure and short-term spikes should not be treated as interchangeable measures.
A strange but familiar unit can make a complex system more legible without making the system simpler.
An index can lose integrity once institutions optimize directly for the measured number.
AI benchmark reports and readiness rankings function as a modern index family even when they are not framed as classical economics.
Owner-built index surfaces can add proof and method context but should not receive editorial priority in the commercial book by default.
